question: True or false: people facing real shocks to live mice diverted the shock onto one more often than people judging on paper?
answer: True. In a 2018 Ghent study, 84% of people who believed the shocks were real pressed the button to spare five mice by shocking one; only 66% of those given the same dilemma on paper said they would. The shocks were secretly harmless. The hand on the button was bolder than the pen.
move: What people say they would do is a separate measurement from what they do.
trap: Expecting real stakes to make people shrink from causing harm.
